item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":131,"end_unit":131,"fact_summary":"Mexico's official multidimensional poverty measure combines income poverty with six social deprivations: education, health, food, social security, housing quality and space, and basic housing services. Official estimates are produced biennially by CONEVAL from INEGI household-survey data, with state estimates every two years and municipal estimates every five years; survey improvements limit direct comparability across some years.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline and measurement limitation; no direct evidence about AMLO's 2023 actions.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["The unit describes measurement methodology and comparability constraints, not 2023 outcomes or government decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":132,"end_unit":133,"fact_summary":"Mexico had a pronounced gender gap in labor-force participation: approximately eight men in ten participated compared with four women in ten. Young women were nearly four times more likely than young men to be NEET, with motherhood identified as a key driver; about 68% of migration abroad was reported as work-related.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline; figures are mainly 2017 or earlier.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["The source does not evaluate policies implemented in 2023 or establish causation by the ruler."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":135,"end_unit":136,"fact_summary":"Formal employment was substantially higher among men, urban residents, and northern states than in southern Mexico; Chiapas and Oaxaca had the lowest formal-employment levels. Nearly all formal employment in the southern region was in the public sector, while about 95% of total employment nationally was generated by the private sector. Women outside the labor market but available for work outnumbered men by more than two to one.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline, using ENOE data through 2017.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["The source provides structural regional and gender disparities, not evidence of AMLO's implementation or correction of them."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":137,"end_unit":139,"fact_summary":"Mexico experienced wage compression toward the bottom between 2005 and 2017: high-wage employment declined, women were disproportionately concentrated at very low wages, and low-paid work was concentrated in rural areas and was mostly informal. Real labor income declined across occupations, genders, and age groups; bottom-40% hourly median wages were stagnant while the top-60% median contracted by about 15%.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline; evidence covers 2005-2017.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["These are historical labor-market trends and do not identify 2023 policy effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":149,"end_unit":150,"fact_summary":"The World Bank benchmarked Mexico against peers and found large gaps from best performers across product and factor markets, public-sector institutions, public-resource allocation, and structural constraints. Aggregate distances were especially high for crime and violence, coordination inefficiencies and investment planning, corruption, access to justice, and human-capital quality.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.10","4B.4","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.5","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline, based largely on 2015-2018 indicators.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["Benchmark distances are comparative diagnostics, not direct measures of AMLO's conduct or 2023 implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":153,"end_unit":155,"fact_summary":"The diagnostic reported weak access-to-justice and rule-of-law conditions, including low judicial independence, weak complaint mechanisms, poor effectiveness and impartiality of criminal investigation and adjudication, high homicide exposure, and poor correctional-system performance. It also reported weak corruption-control indicators, including limited effective checks by courts, legislatures, auditors, and non-governmental actors, and low scores for publicized laws, government data, right to information, and policymaking transparency.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.10","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline, with indicators mainly from 2017-2018.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["The source does not show whether AMLO caused, corrected, or worsened these conditions in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":156,"end_unit":157,"fact_summary":"Mexico's public-resource indicators showed substantial gaps in rural sanitation and drinking-water access, primary and secondary enrollment, rural poverty, and tertiary education. The diagnostic also identified weak fiscal and financial management, low voter turnout in major cities, and deficiencies in meritocratic recruitment, civil-service inclusiveness, and integrity safeguards.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.5","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.7","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline, using indicators primarily from 2014-2017.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["The source reports baseline deficiencies and does not establish 2023 budget execution, appointments, or outcomes under AMLO."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":158,"end_unit":160,"fact_summary":"Mexico's infrastructure and human-capital indicators lagged best performers, including overall infrastructure, roads, electricity, scientific research, education quality, and the share of youth outside employment, education, or training. Environmental indicators showed high exposure to PM2.5 above WHO guidelines, substantial greenhouse-gas emissions, heavy reliance on fossil-fuel electricity, and water stress, alongside relatively low environmental performance.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline, with indicators from 2012-2018.","ruler_attribution":"No attribution to López Obrador is established by this source.","limitations":["The source does not assess AMLO's 2023 environmental, infrastructure, education, or emergency decisions."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is a pre-2023 World Bank diagnostic and mainly describes historical baselines and comparative indicators; it contains no direct evidence about López Obrador's specific 2023 decisions, statements, appointments, implementation, corrections, or outcomes.","No evidence in the supplied units concerns nuclear risk, arms control, international war or peace decisions, or proliferation controls; the document therefore does not support those lenses for 1B or most of 2B."]}
